title: Service operations worklist

intent.summary: Build a runnable service-operations dashboard with a persistent shell, worklist filters, local loading, empty and error recovery states, incident inspection, and an editable record form.

inputs: IncidentWorklist: services, incidents, query, state, selectedIncidentId
adaptation.cancellation: The dashboard owns whether the editor is open. Filters, selection, and the form draft are owned by the dashboard. Cancel closes the editor without clearing the host-owned draft; reopening restores it.
adaptation.simulation: The host owns worklist state (loading, ready, refreshing, or error), query and selected incident ID separately from form submission. Empty and no-match views derive from the available records and query. The local worklist adapter refresh fails once, preserves the current worklist, and succeeds on retry. The local record adapter delays a save, rejects the first save once per application session, and succeeds on retry. Neither adapter makes a network request or sends a notification.

automated: the shell keeps navigation, filters, and the selected incident available while the worklist refreshes
the worklist exposes loading, empty, and error states in its content region and retry preserves the visible worklist
filters refine the local service worklist and an incident can be selected for inspection and editing
invalid submission retains the draft, announces an error summary, and focuses the first invalid field
pending submission makes fields read-only and prevents duplicate submit or dialog closure
failed submission retains the draft and supports retry; successful submission announces local completion
keyboard, narrow layout, reflow, and accessibility checks run in the packed application harness

limitations: The local demo uses deterministic in-memory incidents. It does not model a backend, notifications, offline persistence, concurrent edits, localization, authorization, or production-scale data.
Automation supports runnable readiness only; it does not certify arbitrary consumer adaptations.
